identity.name: UNIPARTS INDIA LIMITED
identity.industry: Off-Highway Components & Precision Engineering for Agriculture, Construction & Aftermarket

summary.oneLiner: Uniparts delivered 14.6% YoY revenue growth and 22.6% EBITDA margin driven by rupee depreciation and Mexico warehouse commissioning, with construction and European Ag outperforming North American Ag; the normalized margin is 18-20%, and FY27 growth is expected to accelerate as markets recover.

one-line thesis: Uniparts delivered 14.6% YoY revenue growth and 22.6% EBITDA margin driven by rupee depreciation and Mexico warehouse commissioning, with construction and European Ag outperforming North American Ag; the normalized margin is 18-20%, and FY27 growth is expected to accelerate as markets recover.
financial scorecard: revenue: Rs.283cr (+14.6% YoY); EBITDA/margin: Rs.63.9cr (+53% YoY), 22.6% (FX-driven; normalized: ~18-20%); PAT (rptd): not disclosed; PAT (normalized): not disclosed; order book: Rs.200cr annualized new awards; net debt: net cash of Rs.226cr
guidance: revenue growth: mid-teen % for FY26; margin: targeting 18-20% normalized EBITDA; order inflow: Rs.200cr annualized new awards; capex/commissioning: Rs.6cr in Q2, Mexico warehouse operational since Oct 2025
order book & pipeline: Rs.200cr annualized new business awards over past 12 months; construction and European Ag driving new wins
segment / subsidiary detail: Construction: 40-45% of revenue, green (strong growth from US AI infra & EU green energy); Large Ag: 17-20%, red in NA (soft), amber in EU (recovering); Small Ag: ~25%, green in Asia/India (GST cut boost), amber in NA (bottoming); Aftermarket: single-digit growth, subdued in EU (inventory), improving in US post-Oct 31 tariff ruling
growth verticals / optionality: Expansion into hydraulics, large fabrications, PTOs via inorganic acquisitions; untapped potential in oil & gas, industrial machinery, mining (under construction segment); Asia and Europe as key growth corridors
margins & cost dynamics: Gross margin expansion driven by 85-90% FX benefit (INR depreciation vs USD/EUR); remaining 10-15% from product mix and tariff pass-throughs; normalized EBITDA margin target: 18-20%
capex / expansion: Rs.6cr in Q2; Mexico warehouse commissioned in Oct 2025; no new capex guidance beyond this
capital allocation: Paid interim dividend of Rs.37.7cr and special dividend of Rs.101.55cr (Rs.22.50/share); net cash position of Rs.226cr; inorganic growth remains strategic priority, no constraint due to strong balance sheet
risks & watch-items: North American large Ag continued softness; global economic slowdown; geopolitical tensions; tariff volatility; rupee appreciation reversing FX benefits
management quality / tone: Confident and strategic; emphasizes operational resilience, dual-shore advantage, disciplined capital allocation, and inorganic growth pipeline; tone is upbeat on construction and European Ag, cautious on NA large Ag
non-obvious takeaways: Mexico warehouse commissioning (Oct 2025) is a hidden catalyst for tariff mitigation and customer retention; 25% flat tariff on tractor parts (Oct 31) is a positive inflection for US aftermarket, not yet priced in

themes.title: Auto components & EV-driveline localization
themes.need: Premiumization, content-per-vehicle rise and EV/hybrid transition pull a deep auto-ancillary chain - MOTHERSON/SONACOMS/BOSCHLTD/SCHAEFFLER/SKFINDIA/UNOMINDA-tier on driveline, bearings, wiring (MSUMI) and EV systems; OLAELEC/ATHERENERG/OLECTRA on EV OEMs (OLAELEC targeting cell-to-pack 10-15% cost edge); SUNDRMFAST/ENDURANCE/CRAFTSMAN/BHARATFORG on forgings/machining. Q1FY27 showed contracted pricing finally landing for Tier-2s: SSWL earned EBITDA/wheel of Rs 314 against Rs 262 YoY, which management attributed mostly to two years of OEM input-price increases finally landing (1-5%, more pending) rather than mix, with all plants above 95% utilisation and knuckles at 100%; KROSS delivered a 12.23% EBITDA margin (+63bps) BEFORE two retrospective pass-throughs land (steel settled ~15 July, the CV conversion-cost settlement still pending), making Q1 a floor rather than a peak.
themes.driver: GST 2.0 demand pull; retrospective OEM price pass-throughs still to land (KROSS CV conversion cost); EV cell/Gigafactory ramps (OLAELEC 6GWh by June); export + new-platform content wins.
